content.text:
Let the transient states track the longest current suffix that is also a prefix of either target pattern:

- \(S_0\): no relevant suffix
- \(S_H\): current suffix is \(H\)
- \(S_{HH}\): current suffix is \(HH\)
- \(S_{HT}\): current suffix is \(HT\)

Absorbing states:

- \(A\): \(HHT\) occurs
- \(B\): \(HTH\) occurs

The transitions are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
\text{State} & H & T\\ \hline
S_0 & S_H & S_0\\
S_H & S_{HH} & S_{HT}\\
S_{HH} & S_{HH} & A\\
S_{HT} & B & S_0
\end{array}
\]

For example, from \(S_{HH}\), another \(H\) leaves the relevant suffix \(HH\), while a \(T\) produces \(HHT\).

---

## Probability that \(HHT\) appears first

Let \(p_0,p_H,p_{HH},p_{HT}\) be the probabilities of eventually hitting \(A=HHT\) before \(B=HTH\), starting from the corresponding states.

The state equations are

\[
p_0=\frac12p_H+\frac12p_0,
\]

\[
p_H=\frac12p_{HH}+\frac12p_{HT},
\]

\[
p_{HH}=\frac12p_{HH}+\frac12(1),
\]

\[
p_{HT}=\frac12(0)+\frac12p_0.
\]

From the first and third equations,

\[
p_0=p_H,\qquad p_{HH}=1.
\]

Also,

\[
p_{HT}=\frac12p_0.
\]

Thus

\[
p_0=p_H
=\frac12(1)+\frac12\left(\frac12p_0\right)
=\frac12+\frac14p_0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac34p_0=\frac12,
\]

so

\[
\boxed{p_0=\frac23}.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{\Pr(HHT\text{ appears before }HTH)=\frac23.}
\]

---

## Expected number of flips until stopping

Let \(E_0,E_H,E_{HH},E_{HT}\) denote the expected additional flips until either pattern appears, starting from each state.

The equations are

\[
E_0=1+\frac12E_H+\frac12E_0,
\]

\[
E_H=1+\frac12E_{HH}+\frac12E_{HT},
\]

\[
E_{HH}=1+\frac12E_{HH}+\frac12(0),
\]

\[
E_{HT}=1+\frac12(0)+\frac12E_0.
\]

From these,

\[
E_{HH}=2,
\]

and

\[
E_{HT}=1+\frac12E_0.
\]

The first equation gives

\[
E_0=2+E_H.
\]

Meanwhile,

\[
E_H
=1+\frac12(2)+\frac12\left(1+\frac12E_0\right)
=\frac52+\frac14E_0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
E_0=2+\frac52+\frac14E_0
=\frac92+\frac14E_0.
\]

So

\[
\frac34E_0=\frac92,
\]

which gives

\[
\boxed{E_0=6}.
\]

Thus the expected stopping time is

\[
\boxed{6\text{ flips}.}
\]
